alignments.note: MACULA tags this בָּ as a plain preposition (R) and supplies no article token beside it, unlike the bracketed [הַ] of 13.5 and 13.15, so it takes only the written in. Follow the morphology rather than the pointing (rule 29).

One substantive rendered by a two-word phrase, with the ASV's supplied the belonging to the nominal expression it determines since no article morpheme is present (rule 15). Head on waste, because places alone is any place (rule 31). The competing reading fuses in the onto the preposition under rule 30, but that rule wants one English rendering of which no morpheme owns a part, and the noun owns this the.
Vocative takes the supplied O into its own unit (rule 36).
Verb with its auxiliary; head on the lexical predicate (rule 24).

review_notes: Corrected: the supplied the (t010) moves from the preposition to the nominal expression. MACULA gives s003 the tag R with no article token of any kind, so no article morpheme is present, rule 30's fusion has nothing to fuse, and rule 15 assigns the supplied the to the noun it determines.

The chapter's other pointed prepositions before a definite noun (13.5 s003/s004, s014/s015; 13.15 s006/s007, s010/s011) do carry bracketed [הַ] tokens, which take the written the under rule 12; this verse is the case where none is supplied.
The ASV reorders the whole verse; units are matched by morpheme, not by position.
